chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang Clears the Cave, Reattaches His Body, and Receives a Dark Offering
chapter_meta_description: A two-hour slaughter clears the Renxiao from the cave. Li Huowang reattaches his lower half, notes the Black Tai Sui’s growing sentience, and receives a pouch of Yang Life Pills from a headless corpse’s final gesture.
og_title: Li Huowang’s Brutal Cave Massacre Ends with a Haunting Offering
og_description: After a close-quarters decapitation of the Daoist Renxiao, Li Huowang leads a two-hour rout, reattaches his body, and watches his parasitic passenger grow smarter. He ends the chapter holding a child in one arm and a pouch of life-pills in the other.
twitter_title: Renxiao Routed, Life Pills Offered: Li Huowang’s Darkest Chapter Yet
twitter_description: A decapitation, a two-hour massacre, and a headless corpse pushing a pouch of life-pills toward the victor—this is Li Huowang’s new normal.

lore_anchors.definition: In the Dao-Twisted World, a Renxiao is a blind, malformed creature created from a person who lives miserably into extreme old age; its hair is long like a shell, its nails are curled, and it speaks only in ghost tongue.
Compressed pellets of raw lifespan, harvested from living beings; they are used as currency for supernatural transactions and as a consumable to extend one’s own remaining years.
A grotesque parasitic entity that, when ingested by a Heart-Element, appears to develop intelligence and communication ability beyond its normal instinctual form.
A military-grade blade imbued with killing intent; its edge is supernaturally sharp and resists common ritual weapons.
A ritual Daoist weapon composed of coins strung on red cord; in the Dao-Twisted World, it can scatter and reform as a tactical combat weapon.
A rare human constitution that makes the bearer valuable as an alchemical ingredient; its flesh may have unique properties that affect parasitic entities.
